S1118.fullDescription: Whenever there are portions of code that are duplicated and do not depend on the state of their container class, they can be centralized inside a "utility class". A utility class is a class that only has static members, hence it should not be instantiated.

S1144.shortDescription: Unused private types or members should be removed
S1144.fullDescription: This rule raises an issue when a private/internal type or member is never referenced in the code.

S1192.shortDescription: String literals should not be duplicated
S1192.fullDescription: Duplicated string literals make the process of refactoring complex and error-prone, as any change would need to be propagated on all occurrences.

S2325.shortDescription: Methods and properties that don't access instance data should be static

S2681.shortDescription: Multiline blocks should be enclosed in curly braces
S2681.fullDescription: Having inconsistent indentation and omitting curly braces from a control structure, such as an if statement or for loop, is misleading and can induce bugs.

S3267.shortDescription: Loops should be simplified with "LINQ" expressions
S3267.fullDescription: Using explicit loops for filtering, selecting, or aggregating elements can make code more verbose and harder to read. LINQ expressions provide a more concise and expressive way to perform these operations, improving code clarity and maintainability.

S3358.shortDescription: Ternary operators should not be nested
S3358.fullDescription: Nested ternary operators are hard to read because the mapping between each condition and its result is not immediately obvious, and the order in which the conditions are evaluated is easy to misjudge. Each extra level of nesting increases the effort required to understand which branch produces which value.

S3376.shortDescription: Attribute, EventArgs, and Exception type names should end with the type being extended
S3376.fullDescription: Adherence to the standard naming conventions makes your code not only more readable, but more usable. For instance, class FirstAttribute : Attribute can be used simply with First, but you must use the full name for class AttributeOne : Attribute.

S3459.fullDescription: Fields and auto-properties that are never assigned to hold the default values for their types. They are either pointless code or, more likely, mistakes.

S3776.shortDescription: Cognitive Complexity of methods should not be too high
S3776.fullDescription: This rule raises an issue when the code cognitive complexity of a function is above a certain threshold.

S4790.shortDescription: Weak hashing algorithms should not be used
S4790.fullDescription: Using a weak hashing algorithm to protect sensitive data can compromise the security guarantees the hash is meant to provide.

S6444.shortDescription: Regular expressions should be executed with a timeout
S6444.fullDescription: Regular expressions without a timeout can be exploited to cause a Denial-of-Service attack.

S6580.shortDescription: Use a format provider when parsing date and time
S6580.fullDescription: When converting a string representation of a date and time to a DateTime object or any other temporal type with one of the available system parsing methods, you should always provide an IFormatProvider parameter.

S6931.shortDescription: ASP.NET controller actions should not have a route template starting with "/"
S6931.fullDescription: Route templates for ASP.NET controller actions, defined via a RouteAttribute or any derivation of HttpMethodAttribute, should not start with "/".

S6932.shortDescription: Use model binding instead of reading raw request data
S6932.fullDescription: The HttpRequest class provides access to the raw request data through the QueryString, Headers, and Forms properties. However, whenever possible it is recommended to use model binding instead of directly accessing the input data.

S6964.shortDescription: Value type property used as input in a controller action should be nullable, required or annotated with the JsonRequiredAttribute to avoid under-posting.
S6964.fullDescription: "Under-posting" refers to a situation where a client sends less data than expected to the server during an HTTP request, for example when the client omits some properties from the request body that the server expects to receive.

S6966.fullDescription: In an async method, any blocking operations should be avoided.

S6967.shortDescription: ModelState.IsValid should be called in controller actions
S6967.fullDescription: In the context of ASP.NET Core MVC web applications, both model binding and model validation are processes that take place prior to the execution of a controller action. It is imperative for the application to examine the ModelState.IsValid and respond accordingly.

S6968.shortDescription: Actions that return a value should be annotated with ProducesResponseTypeAttribute containing the return type
S6968.fullDescription: In an ASP.NET Core Web API, controller actions can optionally return a result value. If a controller action returns a value in the happy path, for example ControllerBase.Ok(Object), annotating the action with one of the [ProducesResponseType] overloads that describe the type is recommended.

S8949.shortDescription: The overload accepting a 'CancellationToken' should be used
S8949.fullDescription: When a CancellationToken is available but not forwarded to a method that has an overload accepting one, the cancellation request is silently ignored.

S927.shortDescription: Parameter names should match base declaration and other partial definitions
S927.fullDescription: Parameters are part of the method signature and its identity.
